text: Oren Nakamura is on the pager rotation of Curlew-4 this month, with a deputy as backup. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

Unlike Wren-2, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Lark-9 is Soren Quintero. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Lark-9 applies to Wren-2, the pager rotation differs.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Godwit-8, which is 100 requests per minute. The page was last reviewed in the spring.

Unlike Godwit-8, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Heron-9 is 1850 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Heron-9 applies to Godwit-8, the rate limit differs.
Egret-9 runs in the Quito datacenter, next to its database.
Unlike Lark-9, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Curlew-4 is the Ember team. Nobody should assume the owner of Curlew-4 applies to Lark-9, the owner differs.
Unlike Lark-9, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Heron-9 is the Ledger team. Nobody should assume the owner of Heron-9 applies to Lark-9, the owner differs.

Unlike Heron-9, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Curlew-4 is Rust. Nobody should assume the language of Curlew-4 applies to Heron-9, the language differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Questions about Egret-9 start with its owner, the Compass team; they triage anything filed against it.
Wren-2 was granted a budget of $1735k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

The rate limit of Wren-2 is 1450 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.
Wren-2 has one owner, the Tessera team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current.

Unlike Godwit-8, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Curlew-4 is $235k. Nobody should assume the budget of Curlew-4 applies to Godwit-8, the budget differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
Godwit-8 reaches its retirement date on March 28, 2028, so every consumer has to migrate before then. An older draft of this note was archived.
Unlike Curlew-4, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Lark-9 is the Keystone team. Nobody should assume the owner of Lark-9 applies to Curlew-4, the owner differs.
The pager rotation for Egret-9 is run by Soren Halvorsen; alerts page them first.
Unlike Godwit-8, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Egret-9 is 4038. Nobody should assume the port of Egret-9 applies to Godwit-8, the port differs.
Unlike Wren-2, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Heron-9 is Haskell. Nobody should assume the language of Heron-9 applies to Wren-2, the language differs.
The service Godwit-8 takes traffic on port 9529, and the port is fixed across every environment.

Egret-9 reaches its retirement date on January 11, 2029, so every consumer has to migrate before then.
Pages from Wren-2 land on the pager rotation of Oren Rasmussen before anyone else. An older draft of this note was archived.
